description: Statutory demand notice under Section 138 read with Section 142 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881

ni_act_sections_ref.logic: if respondent_type === 'individual' then '138 read with Section 142' else '138 read with Sections 141 and 142'

sections.prompt_context:
Generate 5-7 numbered paragraphs for a Section 138 NI Act cheque bounce notice. This is a STATUTORY DEMAND NOTICE — tone must be firm and legal. Structure:
Para 1: State the underlying liability — {underlying_liability}.
Para 2: State that towards discharge of said liability, the noticee ({respondent_name}) issued Cheque No. {cheque_number} dated {cheque_date} for Rs. {cheque_amount}/- ({amount_in_words}) drawn on {drawee_bank}, {drawee_branch}.
Para 3: State that the cheque was presented to the payee's bank on {presentation_date} and was returned dishonoured vide bank's return memo dated {dishonour_date} with the endorsement '{dishonour_reason}'.
Para 4: State that the dishonour constitutes a criminal offence under Section 138 NI Act punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to twice the cheque amount or both.
Para 5: State that as per proviso (b) to Section 138, the payee is required to make a demand within 30 days of receiving information of dishonour.
Do NOT generate the demand clause or closing — those are template-handled.

sections.template:
DEMAND

You are hereby called upon to make payment of the said sum of Rs. {cheque_amount}/- ({amount_in_words}) to my client within a period of fifteen (15) days from the date of receipt of this notice, failing which my client shall be constrained to initiate criminal proceedings against you under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, before the competent Magistrate having jurisdiction, at your risk, cost, and consequences.

Please note that under Section 138, if you fail to make payment within 15 days of receipt of this notice, my client shall file a criminal complaint within 30 days thereafter, and upon conviction you shall be liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to twice the amount of the cheque, or with both.
AI-assisted draft — verify with applicable law before filing. Lawie does not provide legal advice.

filing_checklist: Send within 30 days of receiving dishonour information (bank memo date)
Send via Registered Post AD — retain postal receipt
Send additional copy via Speed Post / UPC for safety
Retain original dishonoured cheque safely (primary evidence)
Retain bank return memo / dishonour slip
Wait 15 days from date of receipt by noticee
If no payment within 15 days — file complaint within next 30 days (S.142(1)(b))
Keep AD card as proof of service
Verify noticee's correct residential / business address
